AccountIn.description:
Connect a new account: the key is validated first; the label defaults to what the
provider reports for the key (Anthropic organization name, OpenRouter key label), else
the provider's name.
AccountIn.title: AccountIn

AccountOut.description:
One provider account of the organization: the console an admin key opens,
with the state of that key. `connected` is per account; a provider is connected when any
of its accounts is.
AccountOut.title: AccountOut

ConnectionOut.description:
The provider's connection as one card: `connected` when any account is, the key fields
of the first connected account, and every account under `accounts`.
ConnectionOut.title: ConnectionOut

EntityLookupOut.description: Which provider (and, once accounts exist, which account) an entity id belongs to.
EntityLookupOut.title: EntityLookupOut

InventorySearchItem.description:
One current inventory resource. A person is one e-mail, so `providers` can list more
than one connector; every other kind is a single identity.
InventorySearchItem.title: InventorySearchItem

KeyCheckOut.description:
The provider's own per-key money (`costs_by_key` run) against the allocated rows per
key; `keys_off` lists the keys outside the one-cent tolerance, largest delta first.
KeyCheckOut.title: KeyCheckOut

OrganizationDeleteIn.description: The slug typed by the owner. It must match the organization in the path.
OrganizationDeleteIn.title: OrganizationDeleteIn

PendingInvitationOut.description: An invitation as the person who received it sees it, on `/me` and the join page.
PendingInvitationOut.title: PendingInvitationOut

PersonIdentityOut.description: One provider account of a person: the inventory row that carries the e-mail.
PersonIdentityOut.title: PersonIdentityOut

ProviderCheckOut.description: Costura total against the provider's own ungrouped total (`cost_total` run).
ProviderCheckOut.title: ProviderCheckOut

QueriesOut.description: One query result per requested measure, in the order the caller named them.
QueriesOut.title: QueriesOut

SetupOut.description:
First-run state of an organization: `connect` while no provider is connected, `ready`
once a month has cost lines, `syncing` in between, `needs_pricing` when Codex is connected
and has no credit price yet.
SetupOut.title: SetupOut

SyncResultsOut.description:
One scheduler run per provider the POST covered: one for a concrete provider, one per
connected provider under `all`. The POST answers before lock acquisition, so every result
is `queued` with no steps; `GET /orgs/{org}/setup` carries the live rows.
SyncResultsOut.title: SyncResultsOut

post.description:
Development stand-in for Google sign-in: any e-mail opens a session, creating the user
on first sight. 403 in production and outside loopback, unless the body is the configured
operator e-mail and secret. 422 on an e-mail without `@`.

get.description: Public capability state; no credential value is returned.

post.description: Create a short-lived, one-use state and PKCE authorization request.
Consume the browser-bound state, exchange the code, verify the ID token, then sign in.

delete.description:
Delete every session of the signed-in user, this one included: the answer to a leaked
or forgotten token.

post.description: Delete the session behind the bearer token; the token stops resolving at once.

Same as accepting, addressed by the token in the join link instead of the id.
A token for another address answers 410 and does not name that address.

Join the organization an invitation names. 410 when it is missing, for another
address, revoked, already used, or expired. The response does not name that address.

get.description:
The signed-in user, the organizations they belong to, the slug of the public sample
organization when seeded (it is not among `organizations`), and the invitations waiting
for this e-mail.

The caller's organizations; the public sample organization and other tenants are not
listed.

schema.title: Response Orgs Api V1 Orgs Get

post.description:
Create an organization with the caller as its owner. 409 on a taken or reserved slug
(`COSTURA_ORG`, `demo`, `demo-staging-*`, `demo-retired-*`), 422 on a slug outside
`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,62}$` or an empty name.

delete.description:
Delete the organization when the body slug matches. 409 while a sync is queued or
running. 422 when the confirmation does not match.

get.description:
One organization the caller can open: a membership, or the public sample organization
(readable without a session, `role` null). 401 without a session elsewhere, 404 when the
slug is unknown or belongs to another tenant.

patch.description:
Change the display name (owner only; 403 on the demo organization). The slug is the
immutable id and is not editable.

schema.title: Response List Credit Prices Api V1 Orgs  Org  Accounts  Account Id  Credit Prices Get

get.description:
Non-completions quantities with billed costs matched by OpenAI cost family. 422 when
the range is reversed, outside 2000-2099 or longer than the range cap. At most `limit`
rows; the `X-Total-Count` header carries how many matched.

schema.title: Response Activity Api V1 Orgs  Org  Activity Get

get.description:
The caller's in-product inbox for one organization: whether they opted in, the newest
50 anomalies since the opt-in with their read mark, and the budget alerts crossed since
the opt-in plus the governance gaps of active keys (`signals`, most money first, 50
listed) with theirs. `unread_count` adds the unread open anomalies and the unread signals;
`unread_by_kind` splits it. Empty and `opted_in: false` on the sample organization and
for a member who has not opted in.

post.description:
Mark inbox items of this organization as read for the caller: the listed anomaly ids
and signals, or every unread item with `all`. Ids of other organizations and signals that
are no longer current are ignored.

put.description:
Opt the caller in to (or out of) the inbox of this organization. Opting in starts the
unread count at the anomalies, budget alerts and key gaps that appear from now on; opting
out clears it.

get.description: How this organization wants spend watched. Defaults when nobody has saved a row.

put.description: Replace the detection settings. Owner only.

get.description:
The organization's audit events, newest first. Owners only (403 for other roles and
on the sample organization). Rows are never updated or deleted, and a reset keeps
them.

Which provider an id belongs to.

`kind` is `key`, `workspace`, `account`, `model` or `anomaly`. The answer comes from the
inventory tables, from the models each provider has billed, or from the anomaly row. 404
when nothing matches. A model name that exists under several providers resolves to
`scope` when it is one of them, else to the provider that billed it most recently.
`account` selects one provider account when the same external id exists on two consoles
of a provider.

Invitations nobody has claimed or revoked, expired ones included so an owner can see
why a link stopped working. Owners only: the list names people outside the organization.

schema.title: Response Organization Invitations Api V1 Orgs  Org  Invitations Get

post.description:
Invite one e-mail address and answer with the link, which is shown once. The link only
works for someone signed in with that address. 409 when the address is already a member or
already invited, 422 when it is not an e-mail.

delete.description:
Withdraw an invitation; its link stops working at once. 404 when it was already
accepted or belongs to another organization.

get.description:
People who can open the organization: owners, then members, then viewers, by e-mail
inside each group. Any member reads it.

schema.title: Response Organization Members Api V1 Orgs  Org  Members Get

patch.description:
Change one person's role. 404 when they are not a member, 409 when the change would
leave the organization without an owner (an owner may step down once another one
exists).

get.description:
Every registered provider with its registry facts and this organization's connection
state; the web builds the scope select and the settings cards from it.

schema.title: Response Providers Api V1 Orgs  Org  Providers Get

get.description: Every account of the provider with the state of its key.

post.description:
Connect one more account of the provider: the key is validated, the account labelled
(`label`, else what the provider reports, else the provider's name) and its first sync
enqueued. 422 when the key already connects another account or the label is taken.

delete.description:
Remove the account with its key and every row synced under it (cost, usage, allocated
lines, inventory, runs, anomalies, projections). 409 while a sync of it is queued or
running.

put.description:
Record what the provider invoiced one account for one month, tax and credits as the
bill shows them. Owner only: it is the figure finance reconciles against. 422 on a
malformed month or a negative amount; 404 on an account of another provider.

delete.description: Forget the account's key; its synced rows stay until the account is removed.

put.description: Replace (or set) the key of one account; the account and its rows stay.
Replace the whole table. 422 on an address that does not look like an e-mail.

get.description:
One anomaly with who to contact, the eight weeks of its series ending on the anomaly
day (baseline samples marked) and the other anomalies of the same day. 404 when the id
belongs to another organization or, under a concrete provider, to another provider.
Configured budgets: the organization total and any workspace, standing across months.

delete.description: Remove the budget and every alert it raised.

put.description:
Create or replace the budget of one scope. A person budget (`person/<email>`) lives
under provider `all` and sums that e-mail across every provider; the organization budget
(`org/__org__`) under `all` sums every provider, its projection included; a workspace
needs one provider (400 under `all`). `period` day or week compares each UTC day or ISO
week with the amount; a person budget is monthly. 422 on an unknown scope kind, a
non-positive amount, a threshold outside 1..200 or a day or week person budget; 404 when
the workspace or the person is not in the inventory.

delete.description:
Forget the key of the provider's only account; 409 with several accounts (disconnect
each through the accounts routes).

put.description:
Validate the key with one provider request, then store it encrypted. Key rejection is
422, temporary upstream failure is 503, an unexpected upstream response is 502, and a
missing COSTURA_SECRET_KEY is 503. Until a scheduler run has succeeded for the account,
storing a key queues its first sync; `first_sync_run_id` names that row. The worker
executes it.

get.description:
Keys by name. `total` counts every matching key; `limit` (at most 2000) and `offset`
page through them.

One key by provider id, missing or not; 404 when the inventory never saw it.

`account` picks one provider account when the same external id exists on two consoles.

Current keys, workspaces, people and services matching `q` in this scope.

`q` is a literal substring of at least two characters. Each kind returns at most
`limit` rows, ranked exact, then prefix, then substring. Missing rows are excluded.
Users and service accounts by e-mail, paged like the key list.
One user or service account. `account` selects among ids reused by two consoles.
Workspaces by name, paged like the key list.
One workspace by provider id. `account` selects among ids reused by two consoles.
Months with at least one cost line, newest first.

Stored anomalies of the month or of the `start..end` days, newest day first and largest
impact inside a day (`sort=impact` orders by impact across days, `sort=severity` by how
abnormal the episode is and then by the money it moved); `open_count` ignores the status
filter but follows the series one, so an entity page counts its own open anomalies.
`open_total` is the same count on any day, for a badge that keeps it across time frames.
`person=<e-mail>` keeps the account series of that person's identities on every provider
in scope. `window_total` is the scope's spend over the same days, so a reader can size an
impact against the period. `total` counts every matching row; `limit` (at most
1000) and `offset` page through them in the chosen order.

Spend against every budget for the month, with the alerts the scheduler recorded.
Spend and percentages are computed on read; alerts are the stored history.
The invoice totals typed in for the month, one per provider account that has one.

Rows of `by` ranked by how much their spend moved against the previous month (its same
days while the month is in progress; for a `start..end` range, the range of the same length
before it), both directions in one list; the overview splits it into rises and falls.

One e-mail across the providers in scope: the inventory accounts carrying it, with the
live keys each created. 404 when no user in scope has the address. The month is part of
the path for the web's scoped URLs only; identities do not depend on it.

Stored month-end projections of the series of one kind; empty for a closed month or
before the scheduler's first `project` step.

Control totals are provider-specific, so the `all` scope answers 400. `?account=`
narrows every check to one account of the provider; without it the checks add the
provider's accounts up. `?reported=` compares with a figure typed into the request;
without it, a calendar month compares with the invoice totals stored for it.
Dollars per day, one series per group in `by` (top N, the rest summed in `other`).
Headline figures: total, previous period, run rate, concentration, cache share.

Tokens and allocated dollars grouped by `by`; filters narrow the lines before grouping.
Under the `all` scope `by=provider` splits the month by connector and `?provider=` keeps
one of them; `by=person` folds one e-mail's direct logins and qualifying Claude Code keys
across providers and `?person=` keeps those personal lines; `by=provider_account` splits
by the console the lines were synced from and `?provider_account=` keeps one.
`format=csv` returns the same rows as `text/csv`.
The contacts assigned by hand to keys and workspaces of this provider.

schema.title: Response List Owner Assignments Api V1 Orgs  Org  Providers  Provider  Owners Get

put.description:
Record who answers for a key or a workspace when the provider inventory names nobody
(or the wrong person). Any member may assign; the anomaly pages read it before the
inventory. 422 on an unknown kind or a malformed e-mail.

get.description: The API keys a member marked as one person's own, on the providers in scope.

schema.title: Response List Personal Keys Api V1 Orgs  Org  Providers  Provider  Personal Keys Get

put.description:
Count a key's spend under one person in the `person` dimension, ahead of the Claude
Code key rule. The address must belong to a user in the organization's provider inventory,
on any provider, so the person row and page exist; 422 otherwise. 404 when the key is not
in the inventory.

get.description:
What needs a person in the scope, most money first: open anomalies of any date and the
budget alerts of the current month. The time frame does not narrow it.

put.description:
Snooze one gap of one key for 7, 30 or 90 days: it leaves the queue, the inbox and the
webhook until then. Snoozing it again moves the date. Owner or member; 404 for a key the
inventory does not hold.

delete.description: Bring a snoozed gap back now. Owner or member.

post.description:
Queue every sync step for the current and previous month and answer 202 with one
queued scheduler run per connected account. The worker runs them; the steps land on the
row as they finish (`GET /orgs/{org}/setup`). Under `all` every connected provider gets
its runs; 400 when none is connected. `?account=` queues one account of a concrete
provider.

get.description:
Several measures of one range, in request order, so a page can fill every series in one
round trip. Bounds match `GET /orgs/{org}/query`. `projection` applies only to
`billed_usd`; every other measure comes back without one.

A bounded date range, bucketed by day, week or month and grouped by up to three
dimensions. Dates are inclusive; `format=csv` returns the same buckets and series in long
form.

Connection state, live runs and newest data. A member's read also requeues runs whose
worker lease has expired (and fails them once attempts are spent). The anonymous read of
the sample organization has no side effect.

post.description: Hide the getting-started card for good; a second call keeps the first timestamp.

Start over as if no key had ever been stored: delete the organization's credentials,
every synced and derived row (`orgs.RESET_TABLES`) and the card dismissal, in one
transaction; other organizations are untouched. The answer is the fresh setup state,
`connect` unless a provider key comes from the environment (ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_KEY,
OPENROUTER_ADMIN_KEY): that key cannot be deleted here, so the state is then `syncing`.

get.description:
Signals of every provider closed in the last 90 days, newest first, with how long each
stayed open. The worker records them every 15 minutes.

Every team with the people, API keys and workspaces mapped to it. A line counts under
its key's team, else its person's, else its workspace's; `by=team` groups spend so.

delete.description: Remove the team with its mappings and its budgets; its spend reads "(no team)".

put.description:
Create the team or rename it. 422 on a slug other than lowercase letters, digits and
hyphens, or an empty name.

Map a person (provider `all`, the e-mail), an API key or a workspace (its provider and
id) to the team; an entity in another team moves. 404 when the team or the entity is not
in the organization.

delete.description: Remove the destination and its delivery history. Owner only.

get.description:
Whether outbound delivery is on for this stack, the host of the saved URL and the 20
newest deliveries (skipped ones left out).

put.description:
Save the HTTPS URL a Slack-compatible webhook listens on, encrypted, with a new signing
secret returned only here. The host must be in COSTURA_WEBHOOK_HOSTS (409 when that list
is empty, 422 when the host is not on it). The first save marks the signals open now as
skipped: only signals that appear afterwards are posted. Owner only.

post.description:
Post one recorded delivery again, rendered from the signal as it stands now (payloads
are not stored), and report whether the destination answered 2xx. The saved host must
still be in COSTURA_WEBHOOK_HOSTS (409 otherwise); 404 for a delivery of another
organization; 422 once the signal closed. A 2xx marks the row sent and puts failed rows
back in the queue, as any successful post does. Owner only.

put.description:
Post a summary of the month, its projection and what needs a person to the webhook on
Mondays (`weekly`) or on the 2nd (`monthly`), or stop (`off`). 422 without a saved
webhook. Owner only.

post.description:
Post a test message to the saved URL now and report whether it answered 2xx. Owner
only.

get.description:
Same database check as /ready, plus the environment name and the API release. Not a
product route.
Process is up. Does not touch the database. Not a product route.
Database is reachable. Not a product route.
